concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
question: Which Act ended the monopoly of the East India Company over trade with India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Charter Act of 1813**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **The Charter Act of 1813** ended the monopoly of the British East India Company over trade in India, except for trade in tea and trade with China.
 
• This Act allowed other British merchants to trade freely with India, marking the beginning of free trade policies.
 
• The Act renewed the East India Company's charter for another 20 years but curtailed its trading privileges, focusing more on administrative functions.
 
• It allocated funds for the promotion of education and authorized Christian missionaries to propagate their religion in India.
 
• The Act also introduced provisions for the expenditure on welfare and education, laying the foundation for modern education in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pitt's India Act of 1784:**

 
 
• This Act aimed to address the shortcomings of the Regulating Act of 1773.
 
• It established dual control over the British East India Company's administration in India by creating a Board of Control in Britain to oversee civil and military affairs.
 
• The Act strengthened British control over Indian administration but did not address trade-related issues.
 
 
 
• **Regulating Act of 1773:**
 
 
• The Regulating Act was the first attempt by the British Parliament to regulate the affairs of the East India Company.
 
• It established the office of Governor-General of Bengal and made provisions for a Supreme Court in Calcutta.
 
• However, the Act did not affect the Company's monopoly over trade in India.
 
 
 
• **Charter Act of 1833:**
 
 
• This Act was significant for administrative reforms and marked the end of the East India Company's commercial activities entirely.
 
• It centralized the administration by making the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India.
 
• The Act also paved the way for legal reforms but was not directly linked to ending the Company's monopoly over trade.
